result.note: Tests the first-ever Indian fuel export to Russia, its routing, the source refinery and the US tariff bill; skips the speculative point about Russia's fuel crisis.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the petroleum shipment from India that reached Russia in early August 2026:
items: It marked the first time Russia had imported fuel from India.
The cargo went through a ship-to-ship transfer off Egypt's Damietta port.
A US bill that names India among buyers of Russian oil authorises tariffs of up to 50% on such buyers.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. The US bill names India among five countries and authorises tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil. The 42,000-tonne cargo took a lengthy detour via Damietta, which suggests Russia's fuel shortage is severe enough to justify paying for supply from South Asia.
questions.source: The shipment marks the first time ever that Russia has imported fuel from India

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Russia received its first-ever fuel import from India. Which refinery shipped the cargo?
questions.explain: The 42,000-tonne shipment came from the Vadinar refinery of Rosneft-backed Nayara Energy, according to data provider Kpler. Nayara has been under European Union sanctions since July 2025.
questions.source: A 42,000-tonne petroleum shipment from Nayara's Vadinar refinery reached Russia in early August, according to data provider Kpler.
